title: Eight Point DFT By Hand Calculator
description: A fully worked 8-point DFT showing every per-sample real and imaginary product, the running sums, and a results table of all eight bins on an exact whole-number example.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
DFT
Numerical Methods

educational.topic: Worked evaluation of the DFT definition
learningObjectives: Explain how the DFT sum produces a specific numeric result
Interpret real, imaginary, and magnitude values per bin
Use the result as a test vector for validating an implementation
prerequisites: Trig values at multiples of pi/4

controls.label: Show all 8 products for this bin
controls.purpose: Expand or collapse the per-sample detail

simulationModel.modelType: Direct evaluation of the DFT definition
equations: X[k] = sum over n of x[n] * (cos(2 pi k n / N) - i sin(2 pi k n / N))
assumptions: N = 8 with a fixed real-valued input
No normalization factor applied to the forward transform
limitations: Different conventions place the 1/N scaling on the forward transform; this one does not, so magnitudes are N/2 times the amplitude

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Fully visible worked example, stepped by bin
keyQuestions: Which bins pair up as mirrors, and why?
commonMisconceptions: That a DFT bin's value is opaque or requires special machinery to obtain
That all N bins carry independent information for a real input
assessmentOpportunities: Predict which bin changes if the DC offset changes from 1 to 3
